item.title: Haiti PM Fils-Aimé names ex-ministers to key posts, fueling criticism over priorities
item.description: Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé appointed some of his former ministers and new officials to ambassadorial and agency roles after a March 20 Cabinet meeting. Critics say the reshuffle reflects political elites' power-sharing and a desire to maintain grip on the country’s meager resources rather than prioritizing security and credible elections amid Haiti’s deepening crisis.

item.title: Air Canada plane collides with fire truck at LaGuardia, killing two and injuring dozens
item.description: An Air Canada jet hit a fire truck at LaGuardia Airport in Queens, New York late Sunday night, killing two pilots and injuring dozens in a runway collision.

item.title: ICE officers go to TSA checkpoints at Trump’s direction, while long wait times at airports persist
item.description: ICE officers deployed at U.S. airports as TSA shortages during shutdown cause long wait times and safety concerns.

item.title: Dozens in Haiti rely on savings groups to access credit where bank loans are unavailable
item.description: In Port-au-Prince, AVÈK savings groups provide members with small loans from collective funds to support businesses and income-generating activities, offering an alternative to banks.

item.title: Residents of Haiti’s Northwest demand completion of airport 20 years in the making
item.description: Residents of Port-de-Paix continue to demand an action plan rather than just words from government officials regarding the construction of an international airport in the region. The National Airport Authority (AAN) announced that a plan is in place to move forward with the project. However, as of Monday, no detailed plan, budget or timeline has been made public.

item.title: Haiti immigration officials detained on passport fraud freed, deny wrongdoing
item.description: Prosecutors released Antoine Jean Simon Fénélon and nine employees of the Immigration and Emigration Directorate after questioning them in a passport fraud investigation.

item.title: At least 70 dead in Haiti’s Artibonite armed gang attack, local rights groups say
item.description: More than 70 people were killed, over 30 injured and dozens of homes burned in an attack in Jean-Denis, Artibonite.

item.title: House reaches 218 signatures to force vote on Haiti TPS for 350,000 migrants
item.description: House reaches 218 signatures to force vote on extending TPS for 350,000 Haitians amid diaspora pressure

item.title: Port-de-Paix prosecutor demands account for missing weapons, drugs, cash, even boat seized
item.description: Jéir Pierre, chief prosecutor in Haiti’s Northwest Department, said missing crucial facts in the seizure of weapons, ammunition and drugs have complicated the work of judges and worsened prolonged detention of suspects. He called for improved collaboration with police, as missing evidence highlights dysfunction and deepens concerns about impunity.

item.title: Federal judge orders improved attorney access at Florida detention center known as “Alligator Alcatraz”
item.description: A federal judge ruled that a Florida detention facility must expand detainees’ access to attorneys, citing barriers to timely legal communication.

item.title: Feds probe whether NYC Council member, Hochul aide took bribes tied to migrant shelter provider | Breaking News
item.description: Federal probe examines alleged bribes tied to NYC migrant shelter funding and BHRAGS contracts.

item.title: Haiti’s new star Isidor scores first goal, but team underwhelms in 1-1 draw with Iceland
item.description: Wilson Isidor, a newcomer from the English Premier League club Sunderland AFC, scored his first goal for Haiti in a 1-1 draw against Iceland, capping a mixed FIFA window. Despite flashes of promise, Les Grenadiers still struggle with midfield control, defensive discipline and consistency ahead of the World Cup.

item.title: Haiti raises fuel prices, but warns against scams to drive black market sales
item.description: Haiti raised fuel prices by up to 40% amid global tensions linked to the U.S. and Israel–Iran war. However, officials say, plenty of fuel is available despite rumors of shortages likely started to drive black market activity.

item.title: Georgia proposal could expand DNA collection from undocumented immigrants in custody for minor offenses
item.description: Georgia bill may allow DNA collection from undocumented immigrants detained for minor offenses, raising legal concerns.

item.title: Coral Springs vice mayor Nancy Metayer Bowen killed in suspected domestic violence case
item.description: A prominent Haitian American elected official in Florida was killed Wednesday, sending shockwaves through the Haitian Diaspora and political circles.
